lines.text: Pounamu is the Māori name for New Zealand greenstone.

lines.text: It is mostly nephrite, found only in the South Island.
The island's Māori name is Te Wai Pounamu, the greenstone waters.
lines.say: The island's MOW-ree name is teh WHY poh-NAH-moo, the greenstone waters.

lines.text: Carvers ground it by hand with sandstone and water.

post.caption: Pounamu pendants were once carved with stone. Pounamu is the Māori name for New Zealand greenstone. It is mostly nephrite, found only in the South Island. The island's Māori name is Te Wai Pounamu, the greenstone waters. Carvers ground it by hand with sandstone and water. Holes were bored with a cord drill tipped with stone. Some pendants were made from old adze blades. Passed down in families, a pendant gains mana, or prestige, with age. A hei matau is a pendant shaped like a fish hook. Legend links the shape to Māui, who fished up the North Island.
